items.note: Put 大都 after a plural subject and before its predicate to say that most members or cases have a property or do something. It does not mean everyone does. Learners often place it after the predicate or confuse it with 都, meaning all.

items.en: They mostly quarrel.
items.wrongPy: tā men chǎo jià dà dōu
items.why: 大都 must come before the predicate; the correct version is 他们大都吵架。

items.note: Use 除非 before a condition and otherwise or 不然 before the consequence: the consequence applies unless the condition is met. Learners sometimes reverse the condition and consequence, but no example phrases are provided here.

Use 把 to place the affected object before the verb, then put the result or other postverbal material after the verb. This pattern presents a cause as bringing about a change. Learners often put the object after the verb; it must follow 把 instead.

未必 goes before a proposition to say that it is not certain or not necessarily true; it does not assert the opposite. Learners often move it after the proposition or mistake it for a definite negation. Keep 未必 before the claim being qualified.

Use 以便 after an action to introduce a subsequent action that the first action makes possible or easier. The action after 以便 is the intended next step. Learners sometimes add 的 after 以便, but this pattern takes the action directly.

items.en: Clean the porcelain so it can be disinfected.
items.wrongPy: qīng xǐ cí qì yǐ biàn de xiāo dú
items.why: 以便 takes the subsequent action directly; the correct version is 清洗瓷器，以便消毒。

items.phrase: 他们交谈以便消除误解
items.zh: 他们交谈，以便消除误解
items.en: They talk so they can clear up the misunderstanding.
items.wrong: 他们交谈，以便的消除误解
items.wrongPy: tā men jiāo tán yǐ biàn de xiāo chú wù jiě
items.why: The action follows 以便 directly, without 的; the correct version is 他们交谈，以便消除误解。

items.note: Put 型 after a compatible feature to label the type, then place the noun being classified after it. Use this pattern for categories such as energy types or manufacturer types. Learners often put 型 before the feature or after the noun.
Use 凡是 before the category condition and 都 before the predicate to state a rule that applies to every case in that category. Learners often put 都 after the verb or predicate, instead of before it.

items.en: Every scenic site is charming.
items.wrongPy: fán shì míng shèng dōu mí rén hěn
items.why: 很 must precede 迷人, so the predicate should be 都很迷人.

items.note: Put 性 after a compatible stem to form a noun for an abstract property or character, as in 毒性 or 弹性. Learners often mistake 性 for a free-standing word and move it away from its stem, or place adverbs in the wrong position.

items.en: The toxicity is strong.
items.wrongPy: dú xìng qiáng hěn
items.why: 很 must precede 强; the correct order is 毒性很强.

items.en: Infectious diseases are contagious.
items.wrongPy: chuán rǎn bìng chuán rǎn xìng yǒu
items.why: 有 must precede its object 传染性, as in 传染病有传染性.

items.note: 总算 goes before the predicate to mark a welcome result reached after difficulty or waiting. It can precede a verb phrase that includes 了. Learners often move 总算 after the verb, where it cannot mark the endpoint in this pattern.

items.en: It's finally his turn.
items.wrongPy: lún dào zǒng suàn tā le
items.why: 总算 belongs before the predicate 轮到他了, not inside it.

items.en: The cultural relics have finally been restored.
items.wrongPy: wén wù xiū fù zǒng suàn le
items.why: 总算 must precede the predicate 修复了, as in 文物总算修复了.

items.en: He finally became well-known.
items.wrongPy: tā yǒu le zǒng suàn míng qi
items.why: 总算 must precede the predicate 有了名气, not split it.

items.en: The wind has finally died down.
items.wrongPy: fēng lì jiǎn ruò zǒng suàn le
items.why: 总算 must precede the predicate 减弱了, not follow it.

items.note: 一再 and 再三 go before a verb phrase to say that an action happens repeatedly, often with emphasis. They do not mean exactly three times. Learners may place them after the verb or between the verb and its object, where they do not form the intended pattern.

items.en: The association revised it repeatedly.
items.wrongPy: xié huì xiū dìng yí zài
items.why: 一再 precedes the verb phrase; the correct order is 协会一再修订.

items.en: The public complained repeatedly.
items.wrongPy: mín zhòng tóu sù yí zài
items.why: 一再 must come before 投诉; the correct order is 民众一再投诉.

items.en: He repeatedly revises the design.
items.wrongPy: tā xiū dìng yí zài tú àn
items.why: 一再 comes before 修订, not between the verb and object; the correct phrase is 他一再修订图案.

items.en: The editor repeatedly questions the order.
items.wrongPy: biān jí zhì yí yí zài mìng lìng
items.why: 一再 must come before 质疑; the correct order is 编辑一再质疑命令.

items.note: Formal 因 introduces a cause and is followed by the resulting predicate, often with a pause between them. Keep the cause after 因 and the complete result after it. Learners can mistakenly move 因 or put a modifier in an impossible position.
就算 introduces a hypothetical concession, and 也 marks the outcome that remains true. Put the condition after 就算 and 也 before the consequence; learners often omit or misplace 也.

items.phrase: 就算前期有漏洞也可行
items.zh: 就算前期有漏洞，也可行。
items.en: Even if there are loopholes at the early stage, it is feasible.
items.wrong: 就算前期有漏洞，也可行也。
items.wrongPy: jiù suàn qián qī yǒu lòu dòng yě kě xíng yě
items.why: The extra final 也 is misplaced; keep 也 before the consequence, as in 也可行.

items.note: 至于 marks a topic shift, followed by the comment about that topic. Keep the topic after 至于 and put the full clause after the comma; learners often move clause particles outside their clause.

Attach 化 after a compatible stem to name a process or resulting state, as in 数字化. It can form a verb or a noun-like expression depending on context. Learners may put 化 before the stem; here it belongs after the stem as a suffix.

items.en: Became more civilized.
items.wrongPy: huà wén míng le
items.why: 化 follows the stem, giving 文明化了.

items.en: Discuss approaches to digitization.
items.wrongPy: tàn tǎo huà shù zì de tú jìng
items.why: 化 follows 数字 to form 数字化, as in 探讨数字化的途径.

items.note: 好不容易 and, in suitable contexts, 好容易 precede a verb phrase to express finally succeeding after difficulty. Keep the verb phrase intact; learners may misread 好容易 as simply easy without context.

到 + endpoint + 为止 marks the inclusive boundary of a period, route, or activity. A clause can follow to say what applies up to that boundary. Learners often reverse 到 and 为止; keep the endpoint between them.

items.phrase: 到港口为止路程很艰难
items.zh: 到港口为止，路程很艰难
items.en: The route is difficult all the way to the port.
items.wrong: 到为止港口，路程很艰难。
items.wrongPy: dào wéi zhǐ gǎng kǒu lù chéng hěn jiān nán
items.why: The endpoint must come between 到 and 为止; say 到港口为止，路程很艰难.

items.note: 明明 comes before a proposition to present it as an evident fact, often contrasting with denial or behavior that contradicts it. Learners may place it after the description; put it before the statement it emphasizes.

A statement-final 嘛 presents a fact or reason as obvious or shared, often with an insistent tone. Use it after the statement, not inside it. Learners may overlook that 嘛 adds a stance rather than simply marking a neutral statement.

特意 and 特地 come before a verb phrase to show that someone acted specifically for a purpose or made a special effort. Use either before the action. Learners often put these adverbs after the verb phrase, where they do not fit Chinese word order.
无 combines with a compatible stem to express the absence of a property or component, often in concise or formal wording. Learners may reverse the order or assume 无 can attach anywhere.

items.en: The crops suffer no disaster.
items.wrongPy: zhuāng jia zāi wú
items.why: 无 precedes the absent condition, so the correct order is 庄稼无灾.

items.en: The home is free from disaster.
items.wrongPy: jiā yuán zāi wú
items.why: 无 must come before 灾; say 家园无灾.

items.en: The guesthouse has no noise.
items.wrongPy: mín sù zào shēng wú
items.why: 无 precedes the thing absent, so the correct phrase is 民宿无噪声.

items.note: Sentence-final 啦 presents an assertion as new, lively, or emphatic, often blending 了 and 啊. Keep it at the end; learners wrongly insert it between a verb and its object.

items.en: I won a prize!
items.wrongPy: wǒ la zhòng jiǎng
items.why: 啦 cannot come before the predicate; put it after 中奖.

items.en: He won a prize too!
items.wrongPy: tā zhòng jiǎng yě la
items.why: 也 is misplaced after the predicate; say 他也中奖啦.

items.note: 一同 comes after a plural subject and before the verb phrase to show that participants act together. It works with a group noun or a subject joined by 和. Learners often place 一同 after the verb; put it before the action instead.

items.en: They study together.
items.wrongPy: tā men niàn shū yì tóng
items.why: 一同 precedes the action rather than following it; say 他们一同念书.

items.en: The general and the ambassador appeared together.
items.wrongPy: jiāng jūn hé dà shǐ chū chǎng yì tóng
items.why: 一同 precedes the action rather than following it; say 将军和大使一同出场.

items.note: 人家 can be the subject meaning other people or a contextually understood person, and it comes before its predicate. Learners may confuse the subject with the object or place 都 after the verb.

items.en: Other people praise him.
items.wrongPy: rén jia tā kuā
items.why: 人家 is the subject and 他 the object; the correct order is 人家夸他。

items.en: People praise her for being resilient.
items.wrongPy: rén jia kuā wán qiáng tā
items.why: 她 must come before the description 顽强; say 人家夸她顽强。

items.note: In this colloquial pattern, 嘛 follows a topic and pauses before a comment about it. Use the pause to frame what the next clause is about. Learners may mistake this topic-marking 嘛 for a statement-final 嘛.

items.en: As for archaeology, it has a lot of depth.
items.wrongPy: kǎo gǔ ma bù hěn yǒu nèi hán
items.why: 不 changes the comment to say archaeology is not very profound; the original says it has a lot of depth.

items.note: 恰好 comes before the predicate to show that something is an exact fit or happens at just the right time. Use it with verbs or descriptions. Learners often put it after 有 or after the rest of the predicate; it should come before the predicate.

items.en: The thief happens to be here.
items.wrongPy: xiǎo tōur zhè qià hǎo zài
items.why: 这 must follow 在 to mark the location; say 小偷儿恰好在这.

items.note: 虽 introduces a conceding fact, followed by a clause that limits its expected consequence; a connector such as 也 or 但 links the second part. Learners often misplace the connectors or put 虽 after the fact.
一向 goes before the predicate to describe a habit or quality that has been consistent over the relevant past. Learners often put it after the predicate; keep 一向 before the verb or adjective.
不禁 comes before a verb phrase to express an involuntary reaction. Learners may move it after the action; keep 不禁 directly before the reaction it introduces.
较为 comes before an adjective to give a qualified, relatively formal assessment. Learners may put it after the adjective or place 也 after 较为; keep 较为 immediately before the adjective.

items.en: The supervisor is relatively fat too.
items.wrongPy: zhǔ guǎn jiào wéi yě féi pàng
items.why: 也 belongs before 较为, not between 较为 and 肥胖.

items.en: His judgment is relatively impressive.
items.wrongPy: tā de yǎn guāng gāo chāo jiào wéi
items.why: 较为 must come before 高超, not after the adjective.

items.note: Use the hurry marker before the whole verb phrase when someone responds promptly to an immediate situation. It does not go after the action or between a verb and its object; learners often place it too late or split the phrase.

items.en: He hurriedly ran away.
items.wrongPy: tā táo pǎo gǎn máng
items.why: The hurry marker is wrongly placed after the action; it belongs before the verb phrase, as in the supplied phrase.

items.phrase: 眼看寒冬赶忙储存花生
items.zh: 眼看寒冬，赶忙储存花生。
items.en: With winter approaching, [we] hurry to store peanuts.
items.wrong: 眼看寒冬，储存赶忙花生。
items.wrongPy: yǎn kàn hán dōng chǔ cún gǎn máng huā shēng
items.why: The hurry marker cannot split the verb from its object; it belongs before the whole verb phrase, as in the supplied phrase.

items.note: 所 + verb + 的 + noun is a formal way to modify a noun, with that noun understood as the verb’s object. It often appears in written or formal Chinese. Learners may put 所 after the verb or omit or misplace 的; keep the whole sequence together.

items.en: The video recording that was collected.
items.wrongPy: sōu jí suǒ de lù xiàng
items.why: 所 must come before the verb, giving 所搜集的录像.

items.note: Place 番 after the numeral that counts an extended bout, following the verb, often with 了 before the numeral. The pattern suits sustained effort, discussion, or performance; learners may reverse 番 and 一 or put 番 before the verb.

items.en: We discuss it for a while.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men yì lùn fān yī
items.why: 番 must follow the numeral in this pattern; reversing the two makes the phrase ungrammatical, unlike the supplied phrase.

items.note: Formal 于 links a time or place to an action: it can come before a verb phrase for time, or after a verb for location. Some verbs also take 于 in fixed patterns, as in 倾向于. Learners often put 于 in the wrong position.

items.en: She works professionally in calligraphy and painting.
items.wrongPy: tā shū huà yú cóng yè
items.why: 于书画 follows 从业 as the location link; the correct order is 她从业于书画.

items.note: Put the frequency adverb before the whole verb phrase to describe an action recurring at intervals. Learners sometimes place it after the action or inside the verb phrase; keep it in front of the complete action.

items.en: He goes offline from time to time.
items.wrongPy: tā xià xiàn bù shí
items.why: The frequency adverb is wrongly placed after the action; it belongs before the verb phrase, as in the supplied phrase.

items.en: They quarrel from time to time.
items.wrongPy: tā men zhēng chǎo bù shí
items.why: The frequency adverb is wrongly placed after the action; it belongs before the verb phrase, as in the supplied phrase.

items.en: The prince periodically avoids the wind and rain.
items.wrongPy: wáng zǐ bù shí fēng yǔ duǒ bì
items.why: The object is wrongly placed before its verb; keep the verb and object together after the frequency adverb, as in the supplied phrase.

items.note: Put 仍旧 or 依旧 directly before the predicate to say an earlier state continues unchanged. Use it for persistence, not a new event. Learners often put it after the predicate; that order is not the standard pattern here.

items.en: The window still has an image.
items.wrongPy: chuāng kǒu yǒu yī jiù tú xiàng
items.why: 依旧 must precede the predicate 有图像; putting it between 有 and 图像 breaks the phrase.

items.note: This 把 construction presents the object as the person or thing that undergoes a resulting state. Use it when an action or event leaves that object changed; learners often mistake 把 for simple physical handling and place the result after the wrong verb.

items.en: The explosion drove everyone to seek help.
items.wrongPy: bào zhà bǎ zhòng rén qiú zhù bī de
items.why: The result phrase must follow 逼得, so the correct order is 爆炸把众人逼得求助.

items.note: Use 一串 for things arranged as a string or cluster, and 一滴 for a small amount of liquid. Learners may choose a measure word by shape alone; check that it fits the kind of thing being counted.

items.en: She has a string of peanuts.
items.wrongPy: tā yǒu yì dī huā shēng
items.why: 花生 cannot be counted as a drop; the phrase uses 一串.

items.note: Use a number followed by 枝 for slender, stem-like objects such as pens, and 扇 for door or window leaves. Learners often choose a measure word by memorizing the noun alone; match the measure word to the kind of object instead.

items.en: There is a window.
items.wrongPy: yǒu yì zhī chuāng
items.why: 窗 takes 扇 here, not 枝; say 有一扇窗。

items.en: This window faces south.
items.wrongPy: zhè zhī chuāng chōng nán
items.why: A window is counted with 扇, so the correct phrase is 这扇窗冲南。

items.en: This is a pen.
items.wrongPy: zhè shì yì shān gāng bǐ
items.why: 钢笔 takes 枝 rather than 扇, so say 这是一枝钢笔.

items.en: One pen is very valuable.
items.wrongPy: yì shān gāng bǐ hěn guì zhòng
items.why: Use 枝 for 钢笔, not 扇; the correct phrase is 一枝钢笔很贵重.

items.note: 除……外 identifies someone or something excluded from the following claim. Use 都 to mark the group covered by that claim; learners sometimes put 都 after the verb instead of before it.

items.en: Everyone except me is there.
items.wrongPy: chú wǒ wài tā men zài dōu
items.why: 都 must precede 在 here, so say 除我外，他们都在.

items.en: Everyone except her gets into a fight.
items.wrongPy: chú wài tā zhòng rén dōu dǎ jià
items.why: The excluded person goes between 除 and 外, so say 除她外，众人都打架.

items.en: Everyone except him argues.
items.wrongPy: chú tā wài zhòng rén zhēng chǎo dōu
items.why: 都 must come before the predicate 争吵, so say 除他外，众人都争吵.

items.note: Use 不料 between two clauses when the second development is contrary to expectation. Keep 不料 at the start of the second clause. Learners may put it inside that clause or rearrange the verb and its subject or object.

items.phrase: 众人播种不料阵雨来临
items.zh: 众人播种，不料阵雨来临。
items.en: Everyone was sowing when, unexpectedly, a shower arrived.
items.wrong: 众人播种，不料来临阵雨。
items.wrongPy: zhòng rén bō zhǒng bú liào lái lín zhèn yǔ
items.why: 阵雨 is the subject of 来临, so it must come before the verb.

items.phrase: 他呆了不料众人也呆了
items.zh: 他呆了，不料众人也呆了。
items.en: He froze; unexpectedly, everyone else did too.
items.wrong: 他呆了，不料众人呆也了。
items.wrongPy: tā dāi le bú liào zhòng rén dāi yě le
items.why: 也 must precede the predicate 呆了, not follow the verb.

items.note: 倒是 goes before the predicate and signals that a fact is noteworthy despite an expectation or contrast. Use it to concede or highlight a point. Learners often put it after the predicate, where it may sound like an afterthought or change the structure.

items.en: She is actually quite relaxed.
items.wrongPy: tā dào shì bú dà fang
items.why: 不 reverses the positive claim; the original says she is 大方.

items.en: The books are actually complete.
items.wrongPy: shū jí dào shì bù qí quán
items.why: 不 reverses the claim; the original says the books are 齐全.

items.en: He is generous toward everyone, though.
items.wrongPy: tā dāi zhòng rén dào shì bú dà fang
items.why: 不 reverses the claim; the original says he is 大方 toward everyone.

items.en: Fine, I'll wait here.
items.wrongPy: dé le wǒ dāi zhè zài ba
items.why: 在 must come before the location 这, so say 得了，我待在这吧。

items.note: 多 + a compatible stem forms a term describing multiple kinds or dimensions, as in 多元. Use it to characterize something as diverse. Learners may reverse the compound and put the stem before 多; keep 多 first.

items.en: The positioning is diverse.
items.wrongPy: dìng wèi yuán duō
items.why: 元多 reverses the fixed 多元 compound; the correct phrase is 定位多元。

items.en: A multilevel system is useful.
items.wrongPy: céng cì de duō tǐ xì yǒu yòng chǔ
items.why: 多 is misplaced inside the phrase; the correct phrase is 多层次的体系有用处。

items.phrase: 多媒体和录像都有用处
items.zh: 多媒体和录像都有用处
items.en: Multimedia and videos are both useful.
items.wrong: 多媒体和录像有用处都
items.wrongPy: duō méi tǐ hé lù xiàng yǒu yòng chǔ dōu
items.why: 都 cannot follow the predicate here; the correct phrase is 多媒体和录像都有用处。

items.note: 反 + a compatible stem forms a term expressing opposition to, or reversal of, what the stem names. Use it as a combined term, such as 反毒. Learners may reverse the parts; keep 反 before its stem.

items.en: He is an anti-drug advocate.
items.wrongPy: tā shì dú fǎn rén shì
items.why: 反 must precede 毒 in this term; the correct phrase is 他是反毒人士。

items.note: This pattern repeats each item around 归 to mark two matters as separate: A has its place, and B has its place. Use it when treating them independently. Learners often omit the second 归; repeat it in both halves.

items.phrase: 高层归高层顾问归顾问
items.zh: 高层归高层，顾问归顾问
items.en: Senior leaders are one thing, advisers another.
items.wrongPy: gāo céng guī gāo céng gù wèn gù wèn
items.why: The second half needs 归 too; the correct phrase is 高层归高层，顾问归顾问。

items.phrase: 管道归管道轨道归轨道
items.zh: 管道归管道，轨道归轨道。
items.en: Pipelines are one thing, and railway tracks are another.
items.wrongPy: guǎn dào guī guǎn dào guǐ dào guǐ dào
items.why: The second half needs 归 too; the correct phrase is 管道归管道，轨道归轨道。

items.note: For book volumes or scrolls, put the number before 卷 and the counted noun after it, as in 三卷文献. 卷 is the volume measure in this pattern. Learners may reverse the order or add another measure word, creating an invalid classifier sequence.

items.en: This is a scroll painting.
items.wrongPy: zhè shì yí huì huà juàn
items.why: The number and 卷 must precede 绘画; the correct order is 这是一卷绘画.

items.note: 净 goes immediately before a verb phrase to say that someone does nothing but the stated activity, often with disapproval. Learners may mistakenly put 净 after the verb; it needs to precede the whole activity.

items.en: He does nothing but report.
items.wrongPy: tā huì bào jìng
items.why: 净 must precede the verb phrase, so 他净汇报 is correct.

items.en: He does nothing but study archaeology.
items.wrongPy: tā kǎo gǔ jìng
items.why: 净 belongs before the activity, not after it.

items.en: She does nothing but lecture me.
items.wrongPy: tā jiào xùn jìng wǒ
items.why: 净 must come before the whole verb phrase 教训我.

items.note: 卷 is the measure word for a roll or scroll and goes after the number or demonstrative and before the noun. Learners may omit it, but a counted noun needs a suitable measure word here.

items.en: One scroll of paintings is large.
items.wrongPy: yí huì huà hěn dà
items.why: A measure word is needed after 一; 一卷绘画 is correct.

items.en: This roll of artwork has marks.
items.wrongPy: zhè huì huà yǒu hén jì
items.why: 这 needs a measure word before 绘画 here; 这卷绘画 is correct.

items.en: He donated a scroll of paintings.
items.wrongPy: tā juān zèng juàn yí huì huà
items.why: The number must come before 卷, so 一卷绘画 is the correct order.

items.note: 干脆 comes before a verb phrase to present a straightforward, decisive choice. It can be followed by particles such as 吧 or 了 in suitable contexts. Learners may place a particle inside the verb phrase; keep the phrase together after 干脆.

items.en: Let's just skip it.
items.wrongPy: gān cuì le miǎn
items.why: 了 cannot go between 干脆 and 免; the correct phrase is 干脆免了。

items.en: Just give feedback.
items.wrongPy: gān cuì ba fǎn kuì
items.why: 吧 belongs after the verb phrase; the correct phrase is 干脆反馈吧。

items.en: I simply endured it.
items.wrongPy: wǒ gān cuì le rěn shòu
items.why: 了 cannot split 干脆 from its verb phrase; the correct phrase is 我干脆忍受了。

items.en: Just divide up the region.
items.wrongPy: gān cuì huá dì yù fēn
items.why: 划分 is the verb and must stay together; the correct phrase is 干脆划分地域。

items.en: Everyone simply scattered.
items.wrongPy: zhòng rén gān cuì sǎn fēn
items.why: 分散 has the order 分 then 散; the correct phrase is 众人干脆分散。

items.en: Let’s simply improve the ventilation.
items.wrongPy: gān cuì qiáng huà ba tōng fēng
items.why: 吧 cannot split the verb phrase 强化通风; the correct phrase is 干脆强化通风吧。

items.note: 超 precedes a compatible descriptive stem to mark an extreme or beyond-normal degree, often in established formations. Learners may treat it like an ordinary degree word and place it after the stem; keep 超 before it.

items.en: This is amazing too.
items.wrongPy: zhè yě shén chāo
items.why: 超 belongs before 神 in this formation, not after it.

items.phrase: 这栋超高层建筑物很高
items.zh: 这栋超高层建筑物很高。
items.en: This super-tall building is very high.
items.wrong: 这栋超高层个建筑物很高。
items.wrongPy: zhè dòng chāo gāo céng gè jiàn zhù wù hěn gāo
items.why: 个 cannot be inserted between the modifier 超高层 and the noun 建筑物.

items.note: 算了 is a set expression for dropping a matter or abandoning an intended action. In these examples it comes before the follow-up; learners may wrongly move 了 into the next verb phrase.

items.en: Buy it up? Forget it.
items.wrongPy: shōu gòu le suàn
items.why: 了算 is not the expression; 算了 is the correct form.

items.en: Forget it; let's stop arguing.
items.wrongPy: suàn le bù le zhēng lùn
items.why: The negation and 了 are misplaced; 不争论了 is correct.

items.en: Forget it; don't export it.
items.wrongPy: suàn le le bù shū chū
items.why: 了 does not precede 不输出; the phrase is 不输出了.

items.en: Let's forget it and not buy it up.
items.wrongPy: suàn le le bù shōu gòu
items.why: 了 is misplaced before 不收购; 不收购了 is correct.

items.note: Place 偷偷 immediately before the verb phrase to describe doing it covertly. It modifies the action, not the subject or its object. Learners often move it after the verb; that does not work in these examples.

items.en: He secretly spat.
items.wrongPy: tā tōu tōu le tù
items.why: 了 cannot go between 偷偷 and 吐 here; the given phrase places it after the verb.

items.note: Put the result expression after a predicate to mark a thorough or extreme result, when that predicate permits this reading. Learners often move the result expression before the predicate or separate its parts; keep it together after the predicate.

items.en: It's extremely tacky.
items.wrongPy: tòu tǔ le
items.why: The result expression must follow its predicate; placing it first breaks the construction, while 土透了 has the correct order.

items.note: Use 特 or 异常 before a gradable predicate to mark a very high degree; 特 is colloquial. Learners often put the degree word after the predicate, where it no longer works.

items.en: Exceptionally significant.
items.wrongPy: xiǎn zhù yì cháng
items.why: This order means “significantly abnormal”; 异常显著 means “exceptionally significant.”

items.en: She has an extraordinary amount of energy.
items.wrongPy: tā yǒu jìn yì cháng
items.why: 异常 precedes the predicate in this pattern; say 她异常有劲.

items.note: 亚 combines with particular established stems to form words meaning below or secondary to a category. It is not freely added to any word; learners may wrongly treat it as a productive prefix.

Use 要么 before each of two alternatives to frame an either-or choice. The alternatives may be short or full actions. Learners sometimes attach 要么 after the first option or repeat it accidentally; keep one 要么 at the start of each option.

Put 也好 after each alternative, then use the shared conclusion after both. This pattern lists options without changing the conclusion that follows. Learners often move 都 away from the conclusion; it belongs before the concluding predicate here.

items.phrase: 线索也好眼光也好都有用
items.zh: 线索也好，眼光也好，都有用。
items.en: Clues or insight, both are useful.
items.wrong: 线索也好，眼光也好，有用都。
items.wrongPy: xiàn suǒ yě hǎo yǎn guāng yě hǎo yǒu yòng dōu
items.why: 都 belongs before the concluding predicate 有用, not after it; say 线索也好，眼光也好，都有用。

items.note: 一时 comes before a predicate to mark a temporary state or action at a particular moment. It does not usually mean “very.” Learners may put it after 很 or split a verb and its aspect marker; keep 一时 before the complete predicate.

items.en: Clear-headed for the moment.
items.wrongPy: hěn yì shí qīng xǐng
items.why: 一时 must come before 很清醒; say 一时很清醒。

items.en: He got caught out for a moment.
items.wrongPy: tā yì shí zhāo zhōng le
items.why: 中招 is the verb phrase and cannot be reversed; say 他一时中了招。

items.en: I got hit by it for a moment.
items.wrongPy: wǒ yì shí le zhōng zhāo le
items.why: 了 cannot precede 中招 here; put it after the predicate, as in 我一时中招了。

items.note: 准 comes before a role or category noun to mean prospective or not-yet-full membership, as in 准主播. It does not mean “certainly” in this position. Learners may omit 是 in a sentence identifying someone; retain it before 准 plus the noun.

items.en: She is a prospective host.
items.wrongPy: tā zhǔn zhǔ bō
items.why: An identifying sentence needs 是 before 准主播; say 她是准主播。

items.en: She is a prospective manager.
items.wrongPy: tā shì zhǔ guǎn zhǔn
items.why: 准 must precede the role noun, not follow it; say 她是准主管。

items.en: The prospective host is here too.
items.wrongPy: zhǔn zhǔ bō zài yě zhè
items.why: 也 belongs before 在 in this sentence; say 准主播也在这。

items.note: Attach the style suffix to a compatible stem to describe a style or method modeled on it, usually before the noun it modifies. Learners often put the suffix before the stem or treat it as a standalone word.

items.en: This is livestream-host-style operation.
items.wrongPy: zhè shì shì zhǔ bō yùn yíng
items.why: The suffix follows 主播, so the correct phrase is “主播式运营,” not “式主播运营.”

items.note: Use the repeated east-one, west-one frame to describe scattered items or occurrences, often with a sense of disorder. Keep the same unit in both halves, and put the numeral before that unit.

items.en: Obstacles are scattered here and there.
items.wrongPy: zhàng ài dōng yí gè xī gè yī
items.why: The numeral must come before 个; the correct ending is “西一个,” not “西个一.”

items.note: Use this expression to concede that a preceding point is valid, often with a sense of agreement. Learners should keep its words in the established order; changing that order can make the expression unnatural or unclear.

Repeat a participant followed by one and an appropriate measure word to distribute successive units among participants. The measure word depends on what is being counted; learners often reverse the numeral and measure word.

items.en: The host gets one, and the manager gets one.
items.wrongPy: zhǔ bō gè yì zhǔ guǎn yí gè
items.why: The numeral must precede 个, so the correct phrase is “主播一个，主管一个.”

items.en: One supervisor, one lead performer.
items.wrongPy: zhǔ guǎn gè yì zhǔ yǎn yí gè
items.why: The numeral must precede 个, so the correct phrase is “主管一个，主演一个.”

items.note: Put the verb before both 这 and 那, repeating it to show the action ranges over different things. Use this pattern for repeated, often impatient activity. Learners may mistakenly put 这 or 那 before the verb.

items.en: She folds this and that.
items.wrongPy: tā zhè zhé zhé nà
items.why: 这 follows the first 折, so the correct order is 她折这折那。

items.en: He burrows here and there.
items.wrongPy: tā zuān zhè nà zuān
items.why: The verb must come before both 这 and 那; the correct order is 他钻这钻那。

items.note: In established paired expressions, 左 comes before the first action and 右 before the second, as in 左转右转. Use the pattern for repeated or all-sided activity. Learners may wrongly treat the paired positions as freely reorderable.

items.en: He turns left and right.
items.wrongPy: tā zhuǎn zuǒ yòu zhuǎn
items.why: 左 must come before 转 in this paired expression; the correct phrase is 他左转右转。

items.en: He turned left and right but still didn’t find it.
items.wrongPy: zuǒ zhuǎn yòu zhuǎn méi zhǎo dào hái shi
items.why: 还是 must introduce the contrasting clause, not follow it; the correct ending is 还是没找到。

items.note: Use 不 + verb + 不 + predicate for the untested state, then 一 + the same verb + 就 to show what happens upon acting. Learners often misplace 一 or 就, which belong together in that order.

items.en: I’m fine when I don’t turn, but I get dizzy as soon as I turn.
items.wrongPy: bù zhuǎn bù yūn yí jiù zhuǎn yūn
items.why: 一 must precede 转 and 就 must follow it; the correct ending is 一转就晕。

items.en: It doesn’t hurt when it isn’t bent, but as soon as it bends, it hurts.
items.wrongPy: bù zhé bù téng yì zhé téng jiù
items.why: 就 must come before the result, not after 疼; the correct ending is 一折就疼。

items.en: If it isn’t pricked, it won’t swell; once it’s pricked, it swells.
items.wrongPy: bù zhā bù zhǒng yí jiù zhā zhǒng le
items.why: 一 must precede 扎 and 就 must follow it; the correct order is 一扎就肿了。

items.note: Use 到 + person + 头上来了 to say that a burden, blame, or unwelcome event has landed on someone. Keep the person between 到 and 头上; learners may put the person in the wrong position.

items.en: Disaster has fallen on him.
items.wrongPy: zāi hài dào tóu shàng tā lái le
items.why: The person must follow 到 and precede 头上; the correct order is 灾害到他头上来了。

items.en: The controversy has landed on me.
items.wrongPy: zhēng yì dào tóu shàng wǒ lái le
items.why: The person must follow 到 and precede 头上; the correct order is 争议到我头上来了。

items.note: 好你个 + person is an emphatic way to address someone with reproach or admiring surprise. Keep 你个 together before the person’s title or description; learners often move 个 after the noun.

items.en: Well, look at you, genius!
items.wrongPy: hǎo nǐ tiān cái gè
items.why: 个 must come before 天才 in this address; the correct order is 好你个天才！

items.en: Well, look at you, host!
items.wrongPy: hǎo nǐ zhǔ bō gè
items.why: 个 must come before 主播 in this address; the correct order is 好你个主播！

items.note: 看把 + person + reaction predicate + 得 exclaims at someone’s pronounced reaction. The reaction predicate comes before 得, and the description after 得 may be left unspoken; learners often put 得 in the wrong place.

items.en: Look how dizzy the host is!
items.wrongPy: kàn bǎ zhǔ bō de yūn
items.why: 得 follows the reaction predicate 晕, so the correct order is 看把主播晕得！

items.en: Look how much pain the host is in!
items.wrongPy: kàn bǎ zhǔ bō de téng
items.why: 得 follows the reaction predicate 疼, so the correct order is 看把主播疼得！

items.note: 早不 + verb，晚不 + the same verb complains that an action happened at an inconvenient time. 不 goes before the verb in both parts; learners sometimes put it after the verb.

items.en: It couldn’t turn earlier or later—why now!
items.wrongPy: zǎo zhuǎn bù wǎn zhuǎn bù
items.why: 不 must precede 转 in both parts; the correct form is 早不转，晚不转！

items.en: Of all times to recruit, why now!
items.wrongPy: zǎo zhāo bù wǎn zhāo bù
items.why: 不 must precede 招 in both parts; the correct form is 早不招，晚不招！

items.phrase: 早不晕晚不晕这时晕了
items.zh: 早不晕，晚不晕，这时晕了！
items.en: It didn’t make me dizzy earlier or later—of all times, it made me dizzy now!
items.wrong: 早晕不，晚晕不，这时晕了！
items.wrongPy: zǎo yūn bù wǎn yūn bú zhè shí yūn le
items.why: 不 must precede 晕 in both parts; the correct form is 早不晕，晚不晕，这时晕了！

items.note: 除非 introduces the necessary exceptional condition, and 才 comes before the consequence. Use it to say that the result happens only if the condition is met; learners often put 才 after the consequence.

items.en: Only if the premier gives instructions will there be governance.
items.wrongPy: chú fēi zǒng lǐ zhǐ shì zhì lǐ cái
items.why: 才 must come before 治理, not after it; the correct order is 除非总理指示，才治理。

items.phrase: 除非主播指示我才转换
items.zh: 除非主播指示，我才转换。
items.en: I’ll switch only if the host tells me to.
items.wrong: 除非主播指示，我转换才。
items.wrongPy: chú fēi zhǔ bō zhǐ shì wǒ zhuǎn huàn cái
items.why: 才 must come before 转换, not after it; the correct order is 除非主播指示，我才转换。

items.note: Use an accomplished event followed by 了就 and the same event followed by 了 to accept what happened and stop dwelling on it. Keep the event words in the same order on both sides; learners may misplace the second 了.

items.en: If it was missed, it was missed.
items.wrongPy: wù le jiù le wù
items.why: The second 了 must follow the repeated event; the correct order is 误了就误了。

items.en: It happened; there’s no use dwelling on it.
items.wrongPy: zhuǎn le jiù le zhuǎn
items.why: The second 了 belongs after 转, so the correct phrase is 转了就转了。

items.note: 放着 + an available thing + 不 + an action describes leaving a resource or opportunity unused, often critically. Put 不 immediately before the action; learners sometimes attach it to the thing or place it after the action.

items.en: Leaving the clues there without checking them.
items.wrongPy: fàng zhe bú xiàn suǒ yàn zhèng
items.why: 不 must precede the action 验证, not 线索; the correct phrase is 放着线索不验证。

items.en: Leaving the obstacle there without removing it.
items.wrongPy: fàng zhe bú zhàng ài pái chú
items.why: 不 must precede 排除, not 障碍; the correct phrase is 放着障碍不排除。

items.en: Leave the energy unused.
items.wrongPy: fàng zhe néng liàng xiāo hào bù
items.why: The negative 不 must come before 消耗, not at the end; the correct phrase is 放着能量不消耗。

items.note: 看 or 瞧 + a personal pronoun + a predicate + 的 forms an exclamation about a visible state or manner, often teasing or reproachful. Keep the pronoun before the predicate; learners may reverse them.

items.en: Look how swollen he is!
items.wrongPy: kàn zhǒng tā
items.why: The pronoun must come before the predicate; the correct exclamation is 看他肿的！

items.en: Look at you working so hard!
items.wrongPy: kàn yòng gōng nǐ
items.why: The pronoun must precede 用功; the correct exclamation is 看你用功的！

items.note: 一时 + one clause, 一时 + another clause presents alternating temporary states or actions. Keep 不 directly before the verb it negates; learners may put it before the subject or after the verb.

items.en: Sometimes it’s swollen; sometimes it isn’t.
items.wrongPy: yì shí zhǒng bù yì shí bù zhǒng
items.why: In the first clause, 不 cannot follow 肿; the correct contrast is 一时肿，一时不肿。

items.phrase: 一时主播在一时主播不在
items.zh: 一时主播在，一时主播不在。
items.en: Sometimes the host is there, and sometimes not.
items.wrong: 一时主播不在，一时不主播在。
items.wrongPy: yì shí zhǔ bō bú zài yì shí bù zhǔ bō zài
items.why: 不 must precede 在, not 主播; the correct contrast is 一时主播在，一时主播不在。

items.note: Use 这也不...那也不... to reject two options in sequence; 这 and 那 can swap order. Put 也不 before each predicate; learners often place 也 after the predicate.

items.phrase: 这也不踏实那也不正规
items.zh: 这也不踏实，那也不正规。
items.en: This isn’t reliable, and that isn’t proper either.
items.wrong: 这踏实也不，那也不正规。
items.wrongPy: zhè tā shi yě bú nà yě bú zhèng guī
items.why: 也不 must come before 踏实; the correct order is 这也不踏实。
